ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Cuthbert is going to make a cube with each face divided into four squares. Each square must have one shape drawn on it; either a cross, a triangle or a circle. Squares that share an edge must have different shapes on them. One possible cube is shown in the diagram. Which of the following combinations of crosses and triangles is possible on such a cube (with the other shapes being circles)?

Each visible face is divided into a 2 by 2 grid, so each face has four small squares, and each small square contains one of the three shapes: a cross, a triangle, or a circle. Reasoning: Since every face of the cube is divided into a 2 by 2 grid, each small square lies at exactly one corner of the cube. At any cube vertex, three small squares meet, one from each of the three faces incident to that vertex. These three squares share edge segments pairwise, so the rule says they must all have different shapes. There are exactly three possible shapes, so each cube vertex must have exactly one cross, one triangle, and one circle. A cube has 8 vertices, and the 24 small squares are partitioned into these 8 vertex triples. Therefore the whole cube must contain exactly 8 crosses, 8 triangles, and 8 circles. Checking the proposed combinations: 6 crosses and 8 triangles would leave 10 circles; 7 crosses and 8 triangles would leave 9 circles; 5 crosses and 8 triangles would leave 11 circles; 7 crosses and 7 triangles would leave 10 circles. None gives 8 crosses, 8 triangles, and 8 circles.

These three squares pairwise share edge segments, so by the text rule they must all have different shapes. Since there are only three shapes, every cube vertex must contain exactly one cross, one triangle, and one circle. A cube has 8 vertices, and the 24 small squares are partitioned by these 8 vertex triples. Therefore the total numbers of crosses, triangles, and circles must each be exactly 8. Check the proposed combinations by adding circles as the remaining squares out of 24; none has crosses = 8 and triangles = 8 and circles = 8, so none is possible.

Add edges between small squares sharing a side, both within each visible-style 2 by 2 face and across cube edges. Then impose a 3-coloring constraint using the three shapes. Either by hand or by a small exhaustive search, assign shapes to the three cells at one cube corner, propagate/check all adjacent inequalities over the cube graph, and record the total count of each shape in every valid coloring. The graph contains 8 disjoint corner triples, and every valid coloring of the graph gives one of each shape in each triple, so the enumeration/count check returns only the total vector 8,8,8. Compare this with the listed options, using circles as the remaining count; each option differs from 8,8,8, so all listed options are impossible.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中显示一个立方体，能看到上、左、右三个面；每个可见面都被分成 2×2 的四个小正方形。每个小正方形中画有三种形状之一：十字、三角形或圆。图中相邻小正方形的形状不同，作为一种可行示例。

再推理：把整个立方体表面建模为邻接图。立方体共有 6 个面，每个面有 4 个小正方形，所以共有 24 个顶点；若两个小正方形共享一条边，就在图中连一条边。每个小正方形必须用三种形状之一着色，且相邻顶点颜色不同。

观察立方体的 8 个角。每个立方体角处恰好有 3 个小正方形相遇，分别来自三个相邻面；这三个小正方形两两共享一条立方体边，因此在邻接图中形成一个三角形 K3。由于只有三种形状，并且相邻的必须不同，所以每个角的这 3 个小正方形必须正好分别是一个十字、一个三角形、一个圆。

这 8 个角对应的三元组互不重叠，并且覆盖全部 24 个小正方形，因为每个 2×2 面上的小正方形都位于该面的某一个角。于是每个角贡献 1 个十字、1 个三角形、1 个圆；8 个角总共只能得到 8 个十字、8 个三角形、8 个圆。

检查给出的组合：6 个十字和 8 个三角形时圆为 10 个；7 个十字和 8 个三角形时圆为 9 个；5 个十字和 8 个三角形时圆为 11 个；7 个十字和 7 个三角形时圆为 10 个。它们都不是 8、8、8 的总数分布，所以都不可能。
